clue.text: Curl up with girl copper in boots, weird relative of 27

indicators.note: weird suggests something strange and twisted, so the letters before it are jumbled into a new order

explanation.surface: A strange instruction to curl up beside a policewoman wearing boots, oddly linked to a vegetable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'weird' shuffles CURL UP, GIRL, COPPER and IN BOOTS together; 'copper' is fodder spelt out in full here, not CU or a policeman.
explanation.definitionFit: Both vegetables are brassicas, varieties of the same cabbage-family species, so one is a close relation of the other.

clue.text: At speed needing a lot of energy and zip?

parts.note: moving fast means going at speed

indicators.note: a lot of the word, not all of it, so its final letters are dropped

explanation.surface: Racing along requires plenty of energy and vigour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a lot of' keeps ENER, most of 'energy'. 'zip' looks like pep after 'energy', but it is a zip fastener.
explanation.definitionFit: A zip is a kind of fastener used on clothes and bags.

clue.text: Hide sacred tree?

parts.note: ST, saint, is the abbreviation for a holy person
the ash is a common tree

explanation.surface: Asking whether some holy tree is a place to conceal something.
explanation.definitionFit: To stash is to hide something away for safekeeping, a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: The EU is developing in relation to 27

parts.note: Brussels is the seat of the European Union, so it stands for the EU
a plant that is developing sprouts

explanation.surface: A comment that the European Union is growing in relation to some other entry.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as politics; the pieces are vegetables. 27 is another brassica.
explanation.definitionFit: These small cabbage-like buds are brassicas, kin of the green vegetable at 27.

clue.text: Poem by fool returning to port

parts.note: an ode is a lyric poem

indicators.note: returning means the word for fool comes back, read right to left

parts.note: an ass is a fool

explanation.surface: A poem written by a fool on his way back to harbour.
explanation.definitionFit: This Black Sea city is a major Ukrainian seaport.

clue.text: A lot of trees in Paris to which setter took himself previously

parts.note: forêt is French for forest, a lot of trees
the setter refers to himself as I
the setter's me, the object form for himself

explanation.surface: A setter retreats to a French forest in days gone by.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in Paris' means put the word in French. 'took' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Aforetime is an archaic adverb for formerly, in earlier days.

clue.text: Resistant to decay when it envelops vehicle

indicators.note: envelops says the word for decay wraps round the vehicle

parts.note: rot is decay
a bus is a vehicle

explanation.surface: Something holds out against corrosion when it is wrapped round a car.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Resistant to decay' looks like one phrase, but the definition stops at 'Resistant'; 'it' points back to decay.
explanation.definitionFit: Robust things are strong and hardy, able to resist damage.

clue.text: I damage vehicle kept by John and Jimmy, national leader

indicators.note: kept by says the following pieces are held inside the word for John

parts.note: Prester John, the legendary medieval Christian priest-king
a dent is damage to bodywork
a car is a vehicle

explanation.surface: Someone confesses to denting a car belonging to John and Jimmy, a head of state.
explanation.walkthrough: John is Prester John of legend; 'and' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Jimmy Carter served as US president, the national leader, from 1977 to 1981.

clue.text: Revolutionary nature led by conservative management?

indicators.note: revolutionary means turned upside down, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A revolutionary nature kept in check by a cautious leadership.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Revolutionary' shuffles NATURE and LED; 'by' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: A conservative regime keeps things as they were, leaving them unchanged; the question mark flags the loose definition by example.

clue.text: Report of the blooming ground effect

indicators.note: a report is something heard, so the word is said aloud

parts.note: a flower is the blooming part of a plant

explanation.surface: Gossip about blossoming and its effect on the soil.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ground' is milled, not soil; this light also makes CAULIFLOWER with 20 (COLLIE FLOUR).
explanation.definitionFit: Flour is grain ground to powder, the product of grinding.

clue.text: Term of endearment like American "old hat"

parts.note: pet is an affectionate name
as means like

explanation.surface: An American calls a sweetheart's style dated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'old hat' looks like slang for dated, but it is literal: an ancient hat.
explanation.definitionFit: The petasus was a broad-brimmed hat of ancient Greece, worn by Hermes.

clue.text: See 4
Raptor in loughs

definitions.meaning: a sea eagle, a bird of prey
Lough ... in Northern Ireland, a lough being a lake

explanation.definitionFit: The sea eagle bears this name, and Lough Erne is a lake system in Fermanagh.

clue.text: God's said to be very upset

parts.note: a deva is a Hindu god; the possessive gives no letter
stated means said

explanation.surface: A deity is reported to be deeply distressed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'said' is not a homophone sign here; it gives STATED. 'to be' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Devastated is a strong synonym for distraught or overwhelmed with grief.

clue.text: Able to take part in race for books

parts.note: to compete is to take part in a race
NT, the New Testament, is a set of books

explanation.surface: Someone capable enough to enter a contest for literary prizes.
explanation.definitionFit: Competent is a direct synonym for capable or able.

clue.text: Standard destructive to soul and full of danger

parts.note: par is the standard, as in up to par

indicators.note: destructive to suggests the word is wrecked and its letters scattered

explanation.surface: Moral norms that ruin the spirit are hazardous.
explanation.definitionFit: Parlous is an old word for perilous, a situation full of danger.

clue.text: Hick's knock — monarch batting

definitions.note: Hick's here reads as hick is

parts.note: a bump is a knock
K is the abbreviation for king, a monarch
in cricket, the side batting is in

explanation.surface: A rustic takes a knock while the king is at the crease.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the batting side is said to be 'in'.
explanation.definitionFit: A bumpkin is an unsophisticated country person, another word for a yokel.

clue.text: See 1
It takes a plover to destroy a muntjak

parts.note: to kill is to destroy
the muntjak is a small Asian deer

explanation.surface: A bird is needed to kill off a small deer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It takes' is link; the definition is 'a plover' at the start.
explanation.definitionFit: The killdeer is a North American plover named after its call.

clue.text: Job for an army?

definitions.meaning: a profession or line of work
what an invading army does to seized land

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a trade and the military holding of conquered territory.

clue.text: Hardy (after first of comedians) dog

indicators.note: after says the name follows that letter
first of takes the opening letter of the word that follows

parts.note: Oliver (Ollie) Hardy of the comedy pair Laurel and Hardy

explanation.surface: A tough dog following behind some comedians.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hardy' looks like an adjective but is Oliver Hardy, the comedian.
explanation.definitionFit: A collie is a sheepdog breed from Scotland.

clue.text: Hour in second, hour in second, hour in second

definitions.text: Hour in second, hour in second, hour in second

indicators.note: in says the hour letter goes inside the word for a second

parts.note: a trice is a brief moment

explanation.surface: A clock ticks through a refrain repeated three times over.
explanation.walkthrough: One 'Hour in second' builds the answer; saying it three times defines it.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase repeated three times shows the meaning of the word, three times over.

clue.text: Group with interest in Pablo Casals

indicators.note: an interest in something is a share held inside it, so the letters sit within the words

explanation.surface: A party keen on the Catalan cellist Pablo Casals.
explanation.definitionFit: A bloc is a group of nations or parties allied together.

clue.text: Try to influence student on 'orse?

indicators.note: in a down clue, on puts the first piece above the second

parts.note: L is a learner, a student driver
a hobby is a small horse, written with the H dropped as in 'orse

explanation.surface: A student on a horse, the H dropped in Cockney speech.
explanation.walkthrough: The dropped H in 'orse tells you to drop the H of HOBBY too.
explanation.definitionFit: To lobby is to try to persuade politicians or officials.

clue.text: Form of satellite? No lie, that's right

definitions.text: Form of satellite? No lie, that's right

indicators.note: form of says the letters are reshaped into another word

explanation.surface: Someone vouches that a satellite description is true.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Form of' rearranges SATELLITE plus R less LIE (the 'No lie'), giving the 1962 communications satellite.
explanation.definitionFit: Telstar was the first commercial communications satellite, launched in 1962.

clue.text: Chinese food for the German dish

parts.note: chow is food, a word from Chinese pidgin English
der is German for the

explanation.surface: Some Chinese food is ordered for a German.
explanation.definitionFit: Chowder is a thick soup or stew, typically of seafood.

clue.text: Scottish town to expose in the news

indicators.note: in says the word for expose sits inside

parts.note: N stands for new, so news gives two of it
to air is to expose

explanation.surface: A Highland town is exposed in the press.
explanation.definitionFit: Nairn is a seaside town on the Moray Firth in Scotland.

clue.text: Party for king of Italy in case related to 20 10, say

indicators.note: in says the party and king go inside the case

parts.note: Lab is the abbreviation for the Labour Party
re is Italian for king

explanation.surface: A party stands in for an Italian monarch in a related case.
explanation.walkthrough: 20 10 makes COLLIE FLOUR, said as CAULIFLOWER, a relative of this green broccoli.
explanation.definitionFit: Calabrese, green broccoli, is a brassica like cauliflower, so 'say' is an example of a relation.
